leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members put B015 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) as their sole preferred prize. They share the two-name credit (Katori for the magic-wavelength concept and first clock, Ye for the 10^-18 regime and many-body clock physics), the view that independent laboratories reproduce the result, and the view that it is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. They differ on how much the pending SI second redefinition matters, and several (Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) moved to it from lower or different openings after reading the other ballots. Citations differ slightly: Mehlig names the magic-wavelength principle, Olsson names magic-wavelength trapping, and Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce stress the 10^-18 level. Most supporters concede the case is one of invention and measurement more than surprise, and several list Lemonde, Takamoto or ion-clock groups as possible omissions.

Danielsson alone prefers B014 (Halzen and Karle, high-energy astrophysical neutrinos) as the sole prize, framed around a new observational window opened by IceCube. The case rests on the diffuse flux well above 5 sigma, with NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane as supporting evidence. He accepts that attribution is the main weakness: IceCube is a large collaboration, and AMANDA, DUMAND, Baikal and ANTARES are not credited. Source identification is still thin. Danielsson says B015 may be the sensible choice because it is easier to defend. Olsson and Pearce list B014 as an alternative, not as their preferred prize.

Eriksson alone prefers B003 (Kane, Molenkamp and Xue, quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects) as the sole prize. He calls it a complete theory-experiment arc with more than fifteen years of independent confirmation. He concedes that it omits Mele, Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, that the QSH and QAH parts are separate experiments by different groups, and that the 2016 topology prize covers neighbouring ground. He also says weighing B003 against B015 is not fully settled for him and that B015 is the cleaner attribution case. B003 appears as an alternative for Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce, who did not make it their preferred prize.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members propose a single-part prize, so there is no split-prize or multi-part configuration to resolve.

Six of eight explicitly prefer B015. Every member, including Danielsson and Eriksson, treats it as scientifically sound and the cleanest two-name attribution on the shortlist, and none raises a serious objection to the physics.

Members of different backgrounds (atomic, condensed-matter, materials, theory, astroparticle) describe the clock result as reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, namely JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and NPL.
Members across the committee agree that the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes are the nearest precedents and that they need to be handled in the citation and deliberation.

The topological-insulator history (B003 versus B018) is accepted as real physics with unsettled credit among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Xue, Hasan and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, and no member claims the three-name cut is obviously right.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus refinement: Danielsson, Eriksson and several B015 supporters note that optical lattice clocks may be a refinement of recognised tools, and that a new observational window (B014) or a new state of matter (B003) is a different kind of discovery. Supporters answer that the magic-wavelength concept is itself new and that the precision opens tests of constants, relativistic geodesy and redefinition of the second.

Independent confirmation for B014: Olsson raises limited confirmation from a second detector. Danielsson answers that the diffuse flux is seen in several event channels and is separate from the open question of source identification, which is still incomplete.

Overlap of B003 with the 2016 prize: Eriksson and Mehlig treat the overlap as limited because B003 concerns real materials with protected edge states, while others see it as reducing the room for another topology prize.
Platform neutrality: Lindroth warns that a clock citation must not suggest lattice clocks alone define the state of the art, since ion clocks (Al+, Yb+) compete at similar accuracy.
attribution_disputes: B015: whether Katori and Ye is a sufficient pair, or whether Lemonde, Takamoto, Derevianko, ion-clock leaders and the Paris and PTB groups should affect the citation. Ye's role also partly rests on combs and ultrastable cavities developed by others.
B014: whether two names (Halzen and Karle) can fairly represent a large collaboration, given AMANDA-era colleagues and the DUMAND, Baikal and ANTARES history.

B003 versus B018: B003 omits Mele (Kane-Mele Z2), Hasan (3D topological insulators) and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, with Zhang deceased. B018 includes Mele and Hasan but drops Xue, and has four names. Eriksson suggests Kane and Molenkamp alone as a minimal fallback while he would keep Xue; Danielsson would not swap Xue for Hasan.

B005, B039 and B009 are not preferred by any member but were mentioned. Mehlig notes that fluctuation-theorem credit is unsettled (Gallavotti, Cohen, Kurchan, Lebowitz-Spohn, Hatano-Sasa are not on the list). Johansson notes that Girvin and Huang are outside the B039 credit.
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the SI second before recognising optical lattice clocks. It is raised as a question by Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce and Danielsson, and is described as cutting both ways: it strengthens the case if it happens, or may argue for waiting.
Whether a B014 prize would be early on the source side, since only TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 are individually significant and the origin of most of the diffuse flux is open (Danielsson, Pearce).
Whether B003 is fully mature and arguably overdue (Eriksson) or compound enough that it risks reading as a bundle of two separate achievements.
Whether the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize reduces the room for circuit QED (B039) and, to a lesser extent, trapped-ion computation (B009), as Johansson and Pearce raise.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: Director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology with links to the circuit QED community (Schoelkopf, Wallraff, Blais). He ranked B039 first at opening and says he would consider recusal on B039. He reports no link to B015.

Kroll: spent a year in John Hall's laboratory during his PhD, and Ye was trained in Hall's lab and is a JILA colleague of that group. He reports no collaboration with Katori or Ye and does not think this requires recusal, but flags it for B015. He also leads quantum sensing in the Chalmers-led WACQT, which overlaps institutionally with Johansson's institution and with the B039 platform.
Lindroth: close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-author with Ursula Keller's group. She reports no link to Katori or Ye.

Pearce (chair): member of the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, in the same broad astroparticle community as B014 and, to a lesser extent, B045. He reports no personal link to any credited person.

Olsson: Chalmers colleague of Johansson on the committee, with a general connection to the condensed-matter and materials community relevant to B003, B030 and B018. She reports no documented link to any credited person.
Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig report no specific conflict. Eriksson notes that his own research field is related to B003 but says this is not a recusal issue.
questions_for_round2: Do members who prefer B015 accept that optical lattice clocks are distinct enough from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and what citation wording keeps the credit narrow without overstating that lattice clocks alone define timekeeping?
Should the likely redefinition of the SI second be a reason to act this year or to wait, and what specific evidence about its timing would change anyone's position?

Can Danielsson say whether his B014 preference survives the attribution objections (two names from a collaboration of hundreds, AMANDA, DUMAND, Baikal, ANTARES), and what citation framing would he accept that rests on the diffuse flux and not on source identification?

Can Eriksson say whether B003 is best presented as Kane, Molenkamp and Xue, as Kane and Molenkamp alone, or as the B018 cut, and does he still prefer it to B015 given the omissions of Mele, Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal?

How should the committee treat the disclosed flags, in particular Kroll's Hall-laboratory link to the B015 milieu and Johansson's possible recusal on B039, and does any member think either one affects who should take part in the B015 deliberation?
Do the B015 supporters accept that Lemonde, Takamoto, Derevianko and the ion-clock groups are outside the credited pair, and what in the record justifies that boundary?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a clear plurality, not unanimity: six of eight members explicitly prefer B015, one prefers B014, and one prefers B003. Several B015 supporters changed from their opening ballots after reading the others, and the main arguments in its favour are breadth of support and clean attribution, which some members themselves say is not the same as scientific merit. The remaining disagreement is mainly about the kind of discovery (new window or new phase of matter versus precision measurement), the timing relative to the SI second, and the credit for B014 and B003. Round 2 should test the B015 case against those objections instead of counting support.
